formal_identities.global_removed_slope: if u=c v for the full syndrome vector, Z=-c makes u+Z v=0, a common-code-line syndrome
formal_identities.pivot_chart: if u=c v on that window, A_T=H(u) ell_T=c H(v) ell_T=c B_T
formal_identities.regular_minor: if u=c v on that window, det((H(u)+Z H(v))_R)=det(H(v)_R)*(Z+c)^(j+1)

local_window_not_global_check.conclusion: local Hankel-window proportionality compresses this exact bucket to one finite slope, but tail moments are needed before charging that slope to the global common-code-line ledger

pivot_slope_checks.identity: A_T=c B_T for every locator/co-support T

regular_minor_checks.expected_shape: zero determinant; proportional branch is still tangent-confined
regular_minor_checks.name: singular_rank_one_minor

theorem.name: Hankel proportional-window root-compression lemma
theorem.statement: For any exact v9 bucket, if u_m=c v_m on the visible Hankel window m<t+j, then H(u)+Z H(v)=(c+Z)H(v) on that bucket. Thus every nonzero regular maximal minor has root set {-c}; every affine pivot slope with B_T nonzero is also -c; and B_T=0 implies A_T=0, hence contained.  If the proportionality holds for the full syndrome vector, then Z=-c is a tangent/common-code-line slope and the branch contributes no aperiodic roots after that ledger is removed.
theorem.v9_residual_label: single_slope; tangent when full syndrome proportional
